informal_statement: Suppose we have a model \( \mathcal{M} \) that satisfies the theory \( T \cup \bigstar \) (where \( \bigstar \) denotes some star operation or modification). Given that \( \mathcal{M} \) models the formula \( \phi \), it follows that \( T \) entails \( \phi \). In other words, whenever a model satisfies a certain composite theory \( T \cup \bigstar \), and the model satisfies \( \phi \), then \( \phi \) must be derivable from \( T \).
informal_proof: First, consider a model \( \mathcal{M} \) that satisfies the theory \( T \cup \bigstar \). By given assumption, since \( \mathcal{M} \) models \( \phi \), we need to establish that \( T \) entails \( \phi \). To do this, we construct an elementary equivalent model based on the structures involved. This step ensures that the truth of \( \phi \) is preserved across equivalent models, which is a fundamental property in model theory. Through this construction, we demonstrate that \( \phi \) holds in every model of \( T \), thereby confirming that \( T \) indeed entails \( \phi \).

Since M can prove all the theorems of U (due to the strong interpretability), it follows that M can also prove all the theorems that U can prove within T. Therefore, M is also a subtheory of T because it possesses all the necessary theorems interpretable within T.

In summary, the strong interpretability of M over U and U being a subtheory of T together imply that M must be a subtheory of T as well.

  /-
    L : LO.FirstOrder.Language
    M : Type w
    inst✝¹ : Nonempty M
    inst✝ : LO.FirstOrder.Structure L M
    T U : LO.FirstOrder.Theory L
    x✝ : LO.System.Subtheory T U
    h : LO.FirstOrder.ModelsTheory M U
    ⊢ ∀ ⦃f : LO.FirstOrder.SyntacticFormula L⦄, Membership.mem T f → LO.Semantics. …
  -/
  intro φ hp
  /-
    L : LO.FirstOrder.Language
    M : Type w
    inst✝¹ : Nonempty M
    inst✝ : LO.FirstOrder.Structure L M
    T U : LO.FirstOrder.Theory L
    x✝ : LO.System.Subtheory T U
    h : LO.FirstOrder.ModelsTheory M U
    φ : LO.FirstOrder.SyntacticFormula L
    hp : Membership.mem T φ
    ⊢ LO.Semantics.Realize inst✝.toStruc φ
  -/
  have : U ⊢ φ := System.Subtheory.prf (System.byAxm hp)
  /-
    L : LO.FirstOrder.Language
    M : Type w
    inst✝¹ : Nonempty M
    inst✝ : LO.FirstOrder.Structure L M
    T U : LO.FirstOrder.Theory L
    x✝ : LO.System.Subtheory T U
    h : LO.FirstOrder.ModelsTheory M U
    φ : LO.FirstOrder.SyntacticFormula L
    hp : Membership.mem T φ
    this : LO.System.Prf U φ
    ⊢ LO.Semantics.Realize inst✝.toStruc φ
  -/
  exact consequence_iff'.{u, w}.mp (sound! ⟨this⟩) M⟩
  /-
    🎉 no goals
  -/

C1_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.sound!
C1_dependencies.content: theorem sound! : T ⊢! φ → T ⊨[Struc.{v, u} L] φ := fun ⟨b⟩ ↦ sound b
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias: theorem sound! : T ⊢! φ → T ⊨[Struc.{v, u} L] φ := fun ⟨b⟩ ↦ sound b

C1_dependencies.name: LO.FirstOrder.consequence_iff'
C1_dependencies.content:
lemma consequence_iff' {φ} :
    T ⊨[Struc.{v, u} L] φ ↔ (∀ (M : Type v) [Nonempty M] [Structure L M] [M ⊧ₘ* T], M ⊧ₘ φ) :=
  ⟨fun h _ _ s _ => Semantics.consequence_iff'.mp h s.toStruc,
   fun h s hs => @h s.Dom s.nonempty s.struc hs⟩
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
lemma consequence_iff' {φ} :
    T ⊨[Struc.{v, u} L] φ ↔ (∀ (M : Type v) [Nonempty M] [Structure L M] [M ⊧ₘ* T], M ⊧ₘ φ) :=
  ⟨fun h _ _ s _ => Semantics.consequence_iff'.mp h s.toStruc,
   fun h s hs => @h s.Dom s.nonempty s.struc hs⟩
